title: A service priced like a supermarket and run like FedEx
lede: Unlike Pets.com, Webvan didn’t spend its way into fame. Its marketing budget was modest. The expensive part was what it promised every customer for free.

rows: Delivery inside a 30-minute window you choose, same day
Dense routing, a fleet of vans and salaried couriers. Couriers were Webvan employees who got two weeks of training, including 36 hours in a classroom[^3]
Free delivery on orders over $50, and no tipping
Delivery cost sat inside G&A, which was 164% of sales in 2000[^3]. In late 1999 the site extended free delivery to all orders through Dec 31[^28]
Prices “generally at or below everyday supermarket prices”
Capped gross margin at grocery levels: 26.5% in 2000[^3]
A store designed to carry over 50,000 items, with hand-cut meat and live lobsters
Large automated centers of 100,000–355,000 sq ft, built before demand[^3]
No second revenue line to subsidize delivery
